qualification.status: Light qualification. Built from this clean Cubature commit as Java 26 bytecode (Temurin 26.0.2.1+1, built in Workbench, where a second build reproduced it byte for byte) with CleanroomGradle against Cleanroom 0.7.14-alpha, from its own compile-only inputs (cleanroom/build-inputs.json); all 347 Java sources in the sources artifact match the commit, and Cubature's own CI passed on it in Workbench: its build inputs, the cleanroom build with its regressions on Java 26, the lab and the tool tests. Its Java sources are those of a970a130: the move to Java 26 changed only build files. Since 30bd6d77 it removes its integration with the game's chunk renderer in cubic worlds, which Quadrature takes over there: a client needs Quadrature as a client mod and without it stops at loading, unless -Dcubature.clientWithoutRenderer=true, under which the game's renderer draws heights 0 to 255 of a cubic world (observability captures without a client mod set it); the count of cubes holding entities kept for the game's entity pass went with that pass. With Quadrature, the forest tour was drawn identically byte for byte on this removal (69e1b2d2) and on 30bd6d77, on copies of one world. No BASELINE capture was run on this pin; the last full qualification, on cbcb09b7, passed a native timing capture and a creative flight lifecycle capture.
qualification.contents: Bounded native generation, regional preparation, previews, storage and DH delivery; host-owned build pools available before biome-provider construction and preserved after adoption; save-level derived-data directory requests; cached cube classification and surface bands, used to install EMPTY cubes without generation and to order delivery visible-first; early initial light and surface tracking for empty sky cubes; retained-column preparation and urgent held teleports; exclusive server-thread phase accounting, with block ticks and player-map bookkeeping separated (the lab alone wraps vanilla call sites for network and tick-event phases), and client native-capture counters; regional preparation around spawn while no player is present; flushes that write each region's backlog in one batch, storage compression on reused deflaters and bounded workers, and regenerable empty cubes left unsaved; a public random-tick listener API on the cubic pass; entity chunk-loading tickets that keep their entity's cube; a client cube source API (versioned snapshots, a held box, a settled signal) with a small client build pool and a client terrain-preview pool that share one governor of work permits, cut on frame and server-tick p95 and raised on queued work, each logging why; a terrain preview's own small build pool, stopped with it; every client pool logging a stop line as its world goes, and counting its threads still alive 1, 2, 5 and 10 seconds after while any is; a client governor that rests while no world is attached; an optional delivery of only the light that changed (off by default); the lab's named reduced view profiles below its baseline, fixed when an instance is prepared; Mixin configurations registered through a CleanMix connector, with MixinExtras wraps and Expressions in place of redirects and constant modifiers; no compatibility code for mods or platforms outside the runtime, no support for clients without Cubature, a client that stops at loading without Quadrature, which draws cubic worlds, no upstream code that nothing calls, of the vanilla generator fixes only those a player can still reach (sapling trees and the huge mushroom), and one build (cleanroom/). Compatibility IDs, packets, save formats and the upstream DH binary are preserved.
limits: Respawn, portal and join arrivals still load their column synchronously
